title: Pointing and noise models change the evidence for an odd shape in 24 HD 139139 dips
abstract: We test a shared odd shape in 24 known HD 139139 dips in K2 campaign 15. A Gaussian shape, a separate timing term for each event, and quadratic pointing terms give a coefficient of 19.45 ppm. Its group-sign tail fraction changes from 0.0508 to 0.125 across noise rules. A two-day local window gives stronger evidence in some groups. Linear pointing terms give a range that includes zero. Removal of the dip marked as suspect in the discovery paper lowers the coefficient to 12.95 ppm. Exposure averaging and synthetic timing checks are included. No shifted control train meets the strict coverage rules, so no time-shift null calibration is available. The evidence depends on the analysis model. We do not confirm a dust tail, a new signal, or a planet. The package contains code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and separate-input retrieval instructions.

display.caption: A fixed odd shape and fitted coefficients under seven models. Ranges use a 10-day group bootstrap. Model and noise choices limit physical interpretation.
